tip: Force the use of IPv4 addresses only.
Force the use of IPv6 addresses only.

option.name: -a
tip: Disable forwarding of the authentication agent connection.

option.name: -A
tip: Enable forwarding of the authentication agent connection.
Can also be set per host in the configuration file.

option.name: -b
tip: Use the given address on the local machine as the source address of the connection.
Only useful on systems with more than one address.

option.name: -B
tip: Bind to the address of the given interface before connecting to the destination host.
Only useful on systems with more than one address.

option.name: -c
tip: Select the cipher specification for encrypting the session.
cipher_spec is a comma-separated list of ciphers in order of preference.
See the Ciphers keyword in ssh_config(5).

option.name: -C
tip: Request compression of all data.
The algorithm is the same as the one used by gzip.

option.name: -D
tip: Specify a local dynamic application-level port forwarding.
ssh acts as a SOCKS server; the SOCKS4 and SOCKS5 protocols are supported.
IPv6 addresses can be enclosed in square brackets.

option.name: -e
tip: Set the escape character for sessions with a pty (default: ~).
The character is only recognized at the beginning of a line.
Set it to none to disable escapes and make the session fully transparent.

option.name: -E
tip: Append debug logs to the given file instead of standard error.

option.name: -f
tip: Go to background just before command execution.
This implies -n.

option.name: -F
tip: Specify an alternative per-user configuration file.
When given, the system-wide configuration file is ignored.
The default is ~/.ssh/config; set it to none to read no configuration files.

option.name: -g
tip: Allow remote hosts to connect to local forwarded ports.

option.name: -G
tip: Print the configuration after evaluating Host and Match blocks, then exit.

option.name: -i
tip: Select a file from which the identity (private key) for public key authentication is read.
Multiple -i options are allowed.
A public key file can be used to name the corresponding private key loaded in ssh-agent.

option.name: -I
tip: Specify the PKCS#11 shared library ssh should use to communicate with a token.

option.name: -J
tip: Connect to the target host through the given jump host.
Multiple jump hops may be separated by commas.
This is a shortcut for the ProxyJump configuration directive.

option.name: -k
tip: Disable forwarding of GSSAPI credentials to the server.

option.name: -K
tip: Enable GSSAPI-based authentication and forwarding of GSSAPI credentials.

option.name: -l
tip: Specify the user to log in as on the remote machine.

option.name: -L
tip: Forward connections from a local TCP port or Unix socket to a host and port on the remote side.
IPv6 addresses can be enclosed in square brackets.
Can also be set with the LocalForward configuration directive.

option.name: -m
tip: Set a comma-separated list of MAC algorithms in order of preference.
See the MACs keyword in ssh_config(5).

option.name: -M
tip: Place the client into master mode for connection sharing.

option.name: -n
tip: Redirect stdin from /dev/null.
This must be used when ssh runs in the background.

option.name: -N
tip: Do not execute a remote command.
Useful for just forwarding ports.

option.name: -o
tip: Give options in the format used in the configuration file.
Useful for options that have no separate command-line flag.
See ssh_config(5) for the options and their values.

option.name: -O
tip: Control an active connection multiplexing master process.
The command is interpreted and passed to the master process.

next.name: cancel
tip: Cancel forwardings.

next.name: check
tip: Check that the master process is running.

next.name: exit
tip: Request the master to exit.

next.name: forward
tip: Request forwardings without command execution.

next.name: proxy
tip: Connect to a running multiplexing master in proxy mode.

next.name: stop
tip: Request the master to stop accepting further multiplexing requests.

option.name: -p
tip: Set the port to connect to on the remote host.
The default port is 22.

option.name: -P
tip: Specify a tag name used to select configuration in ssh_config(5).

option.name: -q
tip: Quiet mode.
Suppress most warning and diagnostic messages.

option.name: -Q
tip: Query the algorithms supported for a feature.
Run ssh -Q help for the supported query terms.
Possible values: cipher, cipher-auth, compression, help, kex, key, key-ca-sign, key-cert, key-plain, key-sig, mac, protocol-version, sig

next.name: cipher
tip: Supported symmetric ciphers.

next.name: cipher-auth
tip: Supported symmetric ciphers that support authenticated encryption.

next.name: compression
tip: Supported compression methods.

next.name: help
tip: Supported query terms.

next.name: kex
tip: Supported key exchange algorithms.

next.name: key
tip: Supported key types.

next.name: key-ca-sign
tip: Valid CA signature algorithms for certificates.

next.name: key-cert
tip: Supported certificate key types.

next.name: key-plain
tip: Supported non-certificate key types.

next.name: key-sig
tip: Supported key types and signature algorithms.

next.name: mac
tip: Supported message integrity codes.

next.name: protocol-version
tip: Supported SSH protocol versions.

next.name: sig
tip: Supported signature algorithms.

option.name: -R
tip: Forward connections from a remote TCP port or Unix socket to the local side.
IPv6 addresses can be enclosed in square brackets.
Can also be set with the RemoteForward configuration directive.

option.name: -s
tip: Request invocation of a subsystem on the remote system.
The subsystem is specified as the remote command.

option.name: -S
tip: Specify the location of a control socket for connection sharing.
Use none to disable connection sharing.

option.name: -t
tip: Force pseudo-terminal allocation.
Multiple -t options force tty allocation even when ssh has no local tty.

option.name: -T
tip: Disable pseudo-terminal allocation.

option.name: -v
tip: Verbose mode; print debugging messages about progress.
Multiple -v options increase verbosity, up to a maximum of 3.

option.name: -V
tip: Display the version number and exit.

option.name: -w
tip: Request tunnel device forwarding with the specified tun devices.
Use the keyword any for the next available tunnel device.

option.name: -W
tip: Forward standard input and output to a host and port over the secure channel.
Implies -N, -T, ExitOnForwardFailure and ClearAllForwardings.

option.name: -x
tip: Disable X11 forwarding.

option.name: -X
tip: Enable X11 forwarding.

option.name: -y
tip: Send log information using the syslog system module.

option.name: -Y
tip: Enable trusted X11 forwarding.
Trusted X11 forwardings are not subjected to the X11 SECURITY extension controls.

option.name: -Z
tip: List the public keys that would be attempted for authentication to the destination, in preferred order, and exit.
